hypotheses.statement: Bounded control flow (for-loops with continue/break, nested loops with inner break, early return from deep nesting) compiles and executes identically under solc/EVM and solang/pallet-contracts at small iteration counts; metering-model divergence, if any, only manifests near gas/weight exhaustion boundaries.

evidence.note: accumulate(10) with continue/break, nested(6,6) with inner break and early return, and all intermediate total() queries matched exactly between backends.

hypotheses.next_probe: Repeat accumulate() and nested() with parameters scaled until EVM runs out of gas mid-loop (e.g., binary-search the largest n that succeeds on anvil), then replay the same sequence on solang and compare status at and around that boundary.

hypotheses.statement: Internal recursive calls (fibRec to depth 8) and revert-inside-loop semantics (revert reason 'loop-revert', full state rollback of total/iterations) behave identically across both toolchains; stack-depth and weight limits rather than semantics are the only expected divergence source.

evidence.note: fib(8) recursion and revertAfter(10) reverting at i==5 produced identical results including revert reason and post-revert total() state.

hypotheses.next_probe: Probe recursion depth limit: call fib(n) with n large enough that EVM approaches the 1024-call-frame stack limit (e.g., a linear-depth recursive counter function recursing 1000+ deep), then compare solang's failure mode (wasm stack trap vs weight exhaustion) and error surfacing.
